entries.summary: Bischof Mangold von Würzburg fällt eine gerichtliche Entscheidung wegen eines Streites, den Kraft von Hohenlohe als Vormund des Sohnes Konrads von Bocksberg mit Heinrich Phal über ein Würzburgisches Lehen zu Gissigheim hatte, das einst dem Juden Anshelm von Lauda versetzt gewesen war.
entries.latin: Manegoldus dei gracia Herbipolensis episcopus tenore presencium notum facimus universis, quod nobis anno domini MCCLXXXVIII° in die sanctorum martyrum Processi et Martiniani iudicio presidente propositum fuit ex parte nobilis viri Kraftonis de Hohenloch, quod Cunradus felicis recordacionis de Bockesberg, avunculus suus, dedisset et obligasset Anshelmo Judeo de Landen in solucionem quorundam debitorum illam decimam in Gisenkein a nobis in feodo descendentem, et cum idem Judeus inhabilis esset ad capiendum feoda, petivit, quod ipsa decima conferretur per predictum Cunradum Heinrico et Theoderico fratribus dictis Pphele, ut portarent nomine feodi ipsam decimam Judeo prelibato, quousque ab ipso eadem decima absolveretur. Postquam autem idem C. de Bokesberg viam universe carnis fuisset ingressus, mortuo eciam ipso Judeo, predictus Krafto de Hohenloch, cui ipsam decimam iure feodali contulimus, nomine tutorio se de ipsa decima intromisit nomine filii supradicti C. de Bokesberg, cuius tutor est et mundibardus. Post hec contencio orta est inter ipsum nobilem et Heinricum Pphal, qui solus superstes fuit, pro decima supradicta; partes vero in arbitros compromittentes a qualibet parte in tres milites, qui arbitri, dum partes concordare non possent, predictam questionem nostro examini tanquam ad dominium feudi remiserunt. Nos vero convocatis ministerialibus ecclesie nostre quesivimus ab eis sub obtentu gracie nostre, que pars pinguius ius haberet in decima memorata; sentenciatum fuit, quod generaliter nullus feoda sua transferre sive conferre posset sine consensu domini sui, a quo eadem feoda descenderent, in aliquas personas minores seu humiliores, et sic ipso iure predicta decima ex morte sepedicti C. de Bockesberg vacaret ab ipso Heinrico Phal et ad nos esset et nostram ecclesiam devoluta. Item sentenciatum fuit, quod cum Judeus, de quo predicitur, mortuus esset, quod Heinricus Phal ammodo portator non esset, sed ab ipso eciam vacaret. Et ex istis sentenciis a nostris ministerialibus promulgatis pronunciavimus, predictum Kraftonem, cui sepedictam decimam contulimus et predecessor noster felicis recordacionis dudum contulerat, nomine tutorio esse verum possessorem prelibate decime, sentencia illorum, qui aderant et requisiti fuerant, approbante. Sunt autem hii ministeriales nostri, qui predictas sententias promulgaverunt: Sintheramus, Eberlinus dictus Hunckelin, Heinricus Wolvolt, Eckelinus scultetus, Beroldus de Hoppherbein, Eberlinus de Randesacker, Heinricus Mulin, Siboto de Walhusen, Siboto de Heithingesvelt, Cunradus pincerna de Randersacker, Eckelinus de Rosseberg, Rapoto de Hohenloch. Actum in curia nostra Hosternache, anno et die ut supra, presentibus Rudolfo de Hurnheim decano, Alberto de Lewenstein scolastico, Wernhero de Tannenberg archidiacono, Ludewico de Hohenberg, Hermanno de Liebesberg, canonicis ecclesie nostre; Hermanno Lezzone, Cunrado de Vinsterloch, Cunrado de Ashusen, militibus; Heinrico de Rebestoch, Heinrico Weibelario, Johanne de Ariete, civibus nostris Herbipolensibus, et aliis quam pluribus ad hoc vocatis et rogatis testibus fide dignis. In evidenciam autem premissorum presentes litteras sigilli nostri patrocinio iussimus communiri pontificatus nostri anno primo.
entries.english: Mangold, by the grace of God Bishop of Würzburg, makes known to all by this letter that, while presiding in judgment in the year of the Lord 1288, on the feast of the holy martyrs Processus and Martinianus, a case was brought on behalf of the noble Kraft von Hohenlohe. He stated that Konrad of Bocksberg, of blessed memory and his uncle, had given and pledged to Anshelm, a Jew of Lauda, in payment of certain debts, the tithe at Gissigheim held in fief from the bishop. Since the Jew was not legally able to hold fiefs, Konrad had asked that the tithe be granted to Heinrich and Theoderich, brothers called Phal, to hold as a fief on behalf of the Jew until the tithe was redeemed from him. After Konrad of Bocksberg had died, and the Jew had also died, Kraft von Hohenlohe, to whom the bishop had granted the tithe as a fief, took possession of it as guardian on behalf of the son of the aforesaid Konrad, for whom he was guardian and protector. A dispute then arose between Kraft and Heinrich Phal, the only surviving brother, over the tithe. The parties submitted the matter to arbitrators, three knights from each side; when the parties could not agree, the arbitrators referred the question to the bishop for judgment as lord of the fief. The bishop summoned his church’s ministerials and asked which party had the stronger right to the tithe. They ruled that no one could transfer or grant a fief to persons of lower status without the consent of the lord from whom the fief derived. Accordingly, by law the tithe became vacant from Heinrich Phal upon the death of Konrad of Bocksberg and reverted to the bishop and his church. They further ruled that, since the Jew had died, Heinrich Phal was no longer its holder and the tithe was also vacant from him. On the basis of these judgments, the bishop declared Kraft, to whom he and his predecessor had previously granted the tithe, to be its true possessor as guardian, with the approval of those present and consulted. The bishop’s ministerials who pronounced these judgments were Sintheramus; Eberlin called Hunckelin; Heinrich Wolvolt; Eckelin, Schultheiß; Berold von Hoppherbein; Eberlin von Randersacker; Heinrich Mulin; Siboto von Walhausen; Siboto von Heidingsfeld; Konrad, cupbearer von Randersacker; Eckelin von Rosseberg; and Rapoto von Hohenlohe. The judgment was made at the bishop’s court at Osternohe, on the aforesaid year and day. Present as witnesses were Rudolf von Hürnheim, dean; Albert von Löwenstein, scholaster; Wernher von Tannenberg, archdeacon; Ludwig von Hohenberg and Hermann von Liebesberg, canons of the bishop’s church; Hermann Lezzone, Konrad von Vinsterloch, and Konrad von Aschhausen, knights; Heinrich von Rebestock, Heinrich Weibelario, and Johannes von Ariete, citizens of Würzburg; and many other trustworthy witnesses summoned for this purpose. In testimony of the foregoing, the bishop ordered this letter to be secured by the protection of his seal, in the first year of his episcopate.

facts.content: pronounced the judgment as one of Bishop Mangold's ministerials.
